issues.legal_issue: An executory maintenance charge over multiple properties remains enforceable against the remaining charged properties after the charge-holder purchases one of them in an earlier execution.
material_facts: A maintenance decree imposed recurring future payments and charged multiple properties for past and future maintenance.
In an earlier execution, the maintenance creditor purchased one of the charged properties subject to the charge.
Further maintenance amounts later became due, and other properties covered by the charge remained available.
issues.conclusion: The earlier purchase did not satisfy or extinguish the charge over the remaining properties; the creditor could execute the decree against those properties for amounts that later became due.
issues.legal_principle: An executory charge-decree for recurring maintenance may be executed again as further sums become due, and the charge continues over all the properties originally charged while the decree subsists. A charge is a right to receive payment out of specified property, unlike a mortgage, which transfers an interest in property; therefore, the mortgage analogy does not apply, and the charge is neither transferred entirely to nor divided by the creditor’s purchase of one charged property. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: maintenance_charge_decree_execution and recurring_payments_become_due and multiple_properties_are_charged and creditor_bought_one_charged_property and other_charged_properties_remain

predicates.maintenance_charge_decree_execution: A creditor sought execution of a decree providing maintenance and charging property to secure payment.
predicates.recurring_payments_become_due: Further maintenance payments became due over time under the decree.
predicates.multiple_properties_are_charged: The decree charged more than one property to secure the payments.
predicates.creditor_bought_one_charged_property: The creditor purchased one property covered by the charge in an earlier execution, subject to the charge.
predicates.other_charged_properties_remain: Other properties covered by the charge remained available after the purchase.

issues.definition: When a maintenance charge decree covers multiple properties, recurring payments become due, the creditor has bought one charged property subject to the charge, and other charged properties remain, the charge remains enforceable against those other properties.

issues.legal_issue: A creditor enforcing a maintenance charge-decree need not first exhaust property that the creditor bought in an earlier execution before proceeding against other charged property held by the debtor.
material_facts: The creditor had purchased charged property in an earlier execution, subject to the maintenance charge.
Further amounts became due under the decree, and the creditor sought to sell other charged properties remaining with the debtor.
The debtor argued that the creditor had to proceed first against the property the creditor had purchased.
issues.conclusion: The creditor could proceed against the remaining charged properties held by the debtor without first proceeding against the property acquired in the earlier execution; the court could choose among the debtor’s properties but could not require the creditor to exhaust the property in the creditor’s possession.
issues.legal_principle: A charge may be enforced against the charged properties jointly and severally, and the law does not require a charge-holder to proceed first against property the charge-holder acquired in execution. The executing court may choose which of the debtor’s charged properties to sell, but it cannot require the creditor to exhaust the creditor’s own acquired property. The court distinguished a charge from a mortgage and relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: maintenance_charge_decree_execution and further_amounts_are_due and creditor_bought_charged_property and creditor_seeks_other_charged_property_held_by_debtor

predicates.maintenance_charge_decree_execution: A creditor sought execution of a decree providing maintenance and charging property to secure payment.
predicates.further_amounts_are_due: Further amounts became due under the decree after an earlier execution.
predicates.creditor_bought_charged_property: The creditor purchased property covered by the charge in an earlier execution, subject to the charge.
predicates.creditor_seeks_other_charged_property_he: The creditor sought sale of other property covered by the charge that remained with the debtor.

issues.definition: When further amounts are due under an executed maintenance charge decree, the creditor has bought charged property, and seeks other charged property held by the debtor, the creditor may proceed against the debtor’s property without exhausting the acquired property.
